messages.subject: Fw: PhD position in evolutionary ecology
messages.body_plain:
From: bounce-5151...@mm.list.cornell.edu <bounce-5151...@mm.list.cornell.edu> on behalf of Reid, Dr Jane M. <jane...@abdn.ac.uk>
Sent: Tuesday, December 3, 2024 16:56
To: euri...@cornell.edu <euri...@cornell.edu>
Subject: PhD position in evolutionary ecology

Hi all,

We have a PhD position available in evolutionary ecology, at NTNU, Norway.

The post is part of a project funded by the European Research Council, which has the overall aim of understanding joint spatial and seasonal eco-evolutionary dynamics.

The aim of the PhD position will be to use a large multi-year capture-mark-recapture dataset to look at links between dispersal and seasonal migration in partially migratory European shags.

The position will provide full training in advanced statistical analyses, with opportunities to contribute to quantitative genetic analyses, theoretical modelling and fieldwork depending on interests.

It’s a fully-funded four-year position, which includes research, courses and teaching components.

The position is open to any nationality conditional on meeting standard European educational requirements (i.e. a 3-year bachelor degree and a 2-year MSc, or another equivalent level of education and/or experience). The working language will be English.

https://www.jobbnorge.no/en/available-jobs/job/271754/phd-candidate-in-evolutionary-ecology

Closing date is January 27th 2025.

Informal enquiries are welcome to Professor Jane Reid (jane....@ntnu.no)

Please forward to anyone who might be interested!

Many thanks for your help,

Jane

The University of Aberdeen is a charity registered in Scotland, No SC013683.

messages.subject: Re: Assistance on State-Space Model Issue
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Just a quick update on this: I made a mistake, and the model works well with total (figure shown below), partial and no overlap of covariates.

Best regards,

Andre

On Sat, Oct 12, 2024 at 10:09 AM André Luís Luza <luza....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Qing Zhao,
>
> Thank you very much for noticing the error! And the Nimble code is really helpful! I will do more tests and check the results.
>
> Have a great weekend.
>
> Best regards,
>
> André
>
> Em sáb., 12 de out. de 2024 09:05, André Luís Luza <luza....@gmail.com> escreveu:
> >
> > Hello,
> >
> > Jags summary did not show any rhat  issue for all simulated data sets. Btw, this model use to converge very quickly (Kery and Schaub 2011, Bayesian Population Analysis using WinBUGS).
> >
> > Best regards,
> >
> > André
> >
> > Em sex., 11 de out. de 2024 22:44, Qing Zhao <white...@gmail.com> escreveu:
> > > Just coded up your model in Nimble and it seems to work fine (with 1 simulation).
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > You can have the Nimble code if you are interested in learning more.
> > >
> > > #===============
> > > # Simulate data
> > > #===============
> > > library(boot)
> > >
> > > n_spp <- 200  # Number of genera
> > > n_bins <- 30   # Number of time bins
> > > n_surveys <- 10  # Number of surveys (geological formations) per time bin
> > >
> > > # Initial occupancy probability
> > > initial_psi <- 0.3
> > >
> > > # Detection probability
> > > p <- runif(n_bins,0,1)
> > >
> > > # covariate effect on origination
> > > intercept_gamma <- logit(0.2)
> > > beta_gamma1 <- 0.5
> > > beta_gamma2 <- 1
> > >
> > > # covariate effect on persistence
> > > intercept_phi <- logit(0.3)
> > > beta_phi1 <- 1
> > > beta_phi2 <- -1
> > >
> > > # covariates (generate just once and save to be used in the other two simulation sets)
> > > X1 <- runif (n_bins-1, -2, 2)
> > > X2 <- runif (n_bins-1, -2, 2)
> > >
> > > phi <- gamma <- array(NA, dim = (n_bins-1)) # persistence, colonisation
> > >
> > > # produce transition probs
> > > for(t in 1:(n_bins-1)){
> > >
> > >   # origination
> > >   gamma[t] <- inv.logit(intercept_gamma + beta_gamma1 * X1[t] + beta_gamma2 * X2[t])
> > >
> > >   # persistence probability
> > >   phi[t] <- inv.logit(intercept_phi + beta_phi1 * X1[t] + beta_phi2 * X2[t])
> > >
> > > } # t
> > >
> > > # Simulate occupancy states
> > > z <- array(NA, dim = c(n_spp, n_bins))
> > > muZ <- array(NA, dim = c(n_spp, n_bins-1))
> > > z[,1] <- rbinom(n_spp, 1, initial_psi)
> > >
> > > # true incidence
> > > for (i in 1:n_spp) {
> > >   for (t in 2:n_bins) {
> > >     muZ[i,t-1] <- z[i,t-1] * phi[t-1] + (1 - z[i,t-1]) * gamma[t-1]
> > >     z[i,t] <- rbinom(1, 1, muZ[i,t-1])
> > >   } # t
> > > } # i
> > >
> > > # Simulate detections
> > > y <- array(NA, dim = c(n_spp, n_bins))
> > > for (i in 1:n_spp) {
> > >   for (t in 1:n_bins) {
> > >
> > >     y[i,t] <- rbinom(1, n_surveys, z[i,t] * p[t])
> > >
> > >   } # t
> > > } # i
> > >
> > > #========================
> > > # Define model in Nimble
> > > #========================
> > > library(nimble)
> > >
> > > code <- nimbleCode({
> > >
> > >   # Priors
> > >   initial_psi ~ dunif(0,1)
> > >   intercept_gamma ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   beta_gamma1 ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   beta_gamma2 ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   intercept_phi ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   beta_phi1 ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   beta_phi2 ~ dnorm(0, sd=10)
> > >   for (t in 1:n_bins) {
> > >     p[t] ~ dunif(0,1)
> > >   }
> > >
> > >   # Process
> > >   for (t in 1:(n_bins-1)){
> > >
> > >     # speciation
> > >     logit(gamma[t]) <-  intercept_gamma +
> > >                         beta_gamma1 * X1[t]+
> > >                         beta_gamma2 * X2[t]
> > >
> > >     # persistence
> > >     logit(phi[t]) <-  intercept_phi +
> > >                       beta_phi1 * X1[t]+
> > >                       beta_phi2 * X2[t]
> > >
> > >   } # t
> > >
> > >   for (g in 1:n_spp) {
> > >
> > >     z[g,1] ~ dbern(initial_psi) # occupancy status initialization
> > >
> > >     for (t in 2:n_bins){
> > >
> > >       muZ[g,t-1] <- z[g,t-1] * phi[t-1] + (1 - z[g,t-1]) * gamma[t-1]
> > >       z[g,t] ~ dbern(muZ[g,t-1])
> > >
> > >     }#t
> > >
> > >   } #g
> > >
> > >   # Observation
> > >   for (g in 1:n_spp) { ## loop over genera
> > >
> > >     for (t in 1:n_bins) { ## loop over time bins
> > >
> > >       y[g,t] ~ dbin(z[g,t] * p[t], n_surveys)
> > >
> > >     } # t
> > >
> > >   } # g
> > >
> > > }) # nimbleCode
> > >
> > > #============
> > > # Run Nimble
> > > #============
> > > # Data
> > > constants <- list(
> > >   n_spp=n_spp, n_bins=n_bins, n_surveys=n_surveys,
> > >   X1=X1, X2=X2
> > > )
> > >
> > > data <- list(
> > >   y=y
> > > )
> > >
> > > # Initial values
> > > inits <- list(initial_psi=0.5,
> > >               intercept_gamma=0, beta_gamma1=0, beta_gamma2=0,
> > >               intercept_phi=0, beta_phi1=0, beta_phi2=0,
> > >               p=rep(0.5,n_bins), z=ifelse(y==0,0,1)
> > > )
> > >
> > > start_time <- Sys.time() # start time of computing
> > >
> > > model <- nimbleModel(code, constants=constants, data=data, inits=inits)
> > > mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(model)
> > > mcmcConf$printSamplers()
> > >
> > > mcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf)
> > > compiled <- compileNimble(model, mcmc)
> > >
> > > fit <- runMCMC(compiled$mcmc, nchains = 3, niter = 5000, nburnin = 0)
> > >
> > > end_time <- Sys.time() # end time of computing
> > > time_taken <- end_time - start_time # computing time
> > > time_taken
> > >
> > > #===============
> > > # Check results
> > > #===============
> > > parms <- c('initial_psi', 'intercept_gamma', 'beta_gamma1', 'beta_gamma2', 'intercept_phi', 'beta_phi1', 'beta_phi2')
> > > parm_values <- c(initial_psi, intercept_gamma, beta_gamma1, beta_gamma2, intercept_phi, beta_phi1, beta_phi2)
> > > fitnms <- colnames(fit$chain1)
> > >
> > > library(rstan)
> > >
> > > par(mfrow=c(3,3))
> > > par(mar=c(2,2,2,1))
> > > for (i in 1:length(parms)) {
> > >   tt <- cbind(fit$chain1[,which(fitnms == parms[i])],
> > >               fit$chain2[,which(fitnms == parms[i])],
> > >               fit$chain3[,which(fitnms == parms[i])])
> > >   diff <- max(abs(tt[2001:5000,] - parm_values[i])) * 1.2
> > >   plot(1, xlim=c(1,5000), ylim=c(parm_values[i]-diff,parm_values[i]+diff),
> > >        type='n', xlab='', ylab='', main=parms[i])
> > >   for (k in 1:3) {
> > >     lines(tt[,k], type='l', col=k+1)
> > >   } # k
> > >   abline(h=parm_values[i], col='grey20')
> > >   text(x=3000, y=parm_values[i]+diff, pos=1,
> > >        labels=paste(c('Rhat = ', format(round(Rhat(tt[2001:5000,]), digits=2), nsmall=2)), collapse=''))
> > > } # i
> > >
> > >
> > > On Fri, Oct 11, 2024 at 2:26 PM Qing Zhao <white...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > In your simulation, you have
> > > >
> > > >             # origination
> > > >             gamma[t] <- plogis(intercept_gamma+beta_gamma1+X1[t]+
> > > >                                       beta_gamma2+X2[t])
> > > >
> > > >             # persistence probability
> > > >             phi[t] <- plogis(intercept_phi+beta_phi1+X1[t]+
> > > >                                     beta_phi2+X2[t])# back to prob scale
> > > >
> > > > Those + should be *.
> > > >
> > > > On Fri, Oct 11, 2024 at 12:43 PM André Luís Luza <luza....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >
> > > > > Hello everyone,
> > > > >
> > > > > While fitting a state-space model to mammal fossil data from the Paleobiology Database, I encountered an issue that I haven’t been able to resolve. During simulations ranging from complete to no overlap of covariates in the models for $\phi_t$ and $\gamma_t$, I found that while the model successfully recovers $\gamma_t$, $\phi_t$, and $p_t$, it struggles to recover the intercepts and regression coefficients for both $\gamma_t$ and $\phi_t$.
> > > > >
> > > > > Below is a figure (with a caption) showing the simulation results for a model with complete covariate overlap. Suspecting potential redundancy between $\gamma_t$ and $\phi_t$, I also tried using an autologistic model with a single parameter $\delta_t$ to summarize the dynamics, but this didn’t improve the results.
> > > > >
> > > > > I won't include code in this email, but you can find a link to my study page below, which provides more context, a detailed description, figures, and the code itself.
> > > > >
> > > > > I have a few questions:
> > > > > Has anyone encountered a similar issue before?
> > > > > Could this problem be due to my use of a Bernoulli-Binomial mixture to model occupancy and detection? Might it be a case of local (rather than global) identifiability, or could it simply be an unnoticed coding error (if you have the time and interest to check)?
> > > > > Are there any references or papers presenting simulations using this mixture model with covariates? I haven’t been able to find any.
> > > > >
> > > > > Any insights would be greatly appreciated!
> > > > >
> > > > > Have a nice weekend.
> > > > >
> > > > > Best regards,
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > André
> > > > > #--------------
> > > > > Github link: https://github.com/andreluza/paleo_macroecology/blob/main/simulations/SIMULATIONS.md
> > > > >
> > > > > Figure:
> > > > >
> > > > > Results illustrating the performance of the model under total covariate overlap. In (A), I show the true values of $\gamma_t$ per time bin $t$ in the X axis, and the estimated values in the Y axis. In (B), I show the true values of $\phi_t$ per time bin $t$ in the X axis, and the estimated values in the Y axis. In (C), I show the true values of $\p_t$ per time bin $t$ in the X axis, and the estimated values in the Y axis. In A-C, the red line depicts the 1:1 relationship of a perfect matching between the truth and the estimated values. One truth-estimate relationship is shown per simulated data set (n=20). In (D), I show violin plots (produced by the 20 simulated data sets) of the intercepts and regression coefficients. The black points depict the true values.
> > > > >
> > > > > --
> > > > > *** Three hierarchical modeling email lists ***
> > > > > (1) unmarked: for questions specific to the R package unmarked
> > > > > (2) SCR: for design and Bayesian or non-bayesian analysis of spatial capture-recapture
> > > > > (3) HMecology (this list): for everything else, especially material covered in the books by Royle & Dorazio (2008), Kéry & Schaub (2012), Kéry & Royle (2016, 2021) and Schaub & Kéry (2022)

Subject: POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER ON BIODIVERSITY MODELLING AND SCENARIO DEVELOPMENT IN EUROPE

Hi

CREAF is seeking an experienced spatial modeller researcher with a strong background in spatial biodiversity modelling and use of scenario projections to work, together with other European institutions, on building novel future projections of biodiversity aimed at capturing future spatial dynamics of bird distributions under different scenarios at different spatial scales (from subnational to European). These novel projections will explore IPBES based Nature Positive Futures including re-wilding (recovering of natural processes at the system level).

More info:
